question.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(3,-3)$ lies on the curve $y=3f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=f(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
The function $y=3f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $3$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $3.$

The point $Q(3,q)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $P(3,-3)$ on $y=3f(x).$ Since we know that the $y$-coordinate of $P$ is $3$ times the $y$-coordinate of $Q,$ we can form the following equation:

$$
3q=-3
$$

Solving this equation, we get $q=-1.$ Therefore, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(3,-1).$
